core_principles: Append-only: a line is never edited. A correction is a NEW record with event=correction that supersedes an earlier id. This is the no-backfill doctrine in machine form.

Two separate streams, .MD and .JSONL, complementary - neither is the source or the rendering of the other. They interlock by timestamps, by shared vocabularies, by citable record ids, and by the same qualitative content. (Settled in the logging deliberation of 2026-10-17, 23:02-23:36 EDT; this replaces the proposal's one-source principle.)
Distributed: each repo, workspace or channel may keep its own shard (its own .jsonl file) under this same schema. Shards merge by id and ts; no central file is required.

Qualitative first: the lived reading (summary, qualia, aesthetic problem/solution) is in the operator's first person. Numbers live only in the optional derived block and are labelled as derived - they support a reading, they never replace it.
Provenance on every record: what the time rests on, what sources were used, and which commit / file / refcard the event touches.

dictionaries._what: Separate versioned dictionary files. Records stay compact; dictionaries carry the definitions. A dictionary is itself append-only JSONL: a term is added by a record, superseded by a later record, never edited.
dictionaries.aesthetic_problems: problem_id, statement, opened_in (record id), status (open | solved | abandoned), solved_in (record id or null)
dictionaries.projects: project slugs as already used in frontmatter
dictionaries.qualia: QoT adjectives; each entry: term, definition in Alex's work terms, introduced (date), first_used (record id / context), status (proposed | adopted)
dictionaries.session_types: existing controlled vocabulary, carried over unchanged
dictionaries.workspaces: existing controlled vocabulary, carried over unchanged

format: NDJSON / JSONL: one JSON object per line, no pretty-printing, no literal newlines inside a record, append-only
open_decisions_for_alex: One shard file per repo/workspace, or session files (like the first official log, one evening file with per-record shard tags) merged at snapshot time? Alpha practice: session files.
Does temperature_vector appear per segment, per snapshot only, or both?
Which event types from the list survive, in his words?
Does record_hash return in beta, or does the prev_hash chain plus git suffice?

aesthetic._what: The aesthetic operation, logged as data: problems and their elegant solutions carry provenance like anything else.
discarded: alternatives considered and set aside, with the reason in one phrase
aesthetic.elegance: why this solution is elegant, in qualitative terms
aesthetic.problem: the aesthetic problem as stated by the operator
aesthetic.problem_id: stable id, e.g. ap-2026-014, so a solution months later can link back
aesthetic.solution: the elegant solution, when found (may be in a later record)
aesthetic.tension: what makes it a problem - the friction, the unresolved pull

context.channel: where the work happened, if a channel
context.place: free qualitative place note, e.g. in the field (a place note can qualify a workspace, by the operator's ruling)
context.session_type: list, the verb: [research, discourse, publishing, reading, composing, painting, ...] - orthogonal to workspace; workspace x session_type = the active space
context.stream: list: [image, sound, text] - code is text unless Alex rules otherwise
context.workspace: list, the place: [studio, lab, field, cemetery, ...] - open vocabulary, extend by proposal only

delta.summary: one line, first person, the appreciable change - what is new, moved, gone

derived._what: OPTIONAL, machine-computed only, always labelled derived: counts that support a temperature reading (messages in window, commits, repos touched, switches). Never presented as the experience itself - the record is not the experience.

optional_blocks.properties: event-specific bag, different keys per event type - exactly as in analytics JSONL. Variability here is normal and is why this is JSONL, not CSV.

commit.hash: full commit hash from the real version history

provenance.prev_hash: sha256 of the previous line exactly as written - the hash chain that makes the append-only ledger tamper-evident
provenance.record_hash: OMITTED in alpha: integrity is carried by the next record's prev_hash (the chain) and by the git history. Whether record_hash returns is a beta decision.

snapshot._what: Only on event=snapshot. The snapshot freezes the whole surface at departure (snapshot doctrine).
snapshot.unrecorded: what the operator knows happened off-record - named honestly instead of reconstructed silently

span.time_basis: channel timestamps | file timestamps | commit timestamps | operator report - REQUIRED whenever a span is stated (time-honesty rule)

temperature_vector._what: Delta-W temperature as a VECTOR, not a scalar: one qualitative reading per workspace / project dimension, so a snapshot can render the whole surface at once (tonal cinema). No numbers required.

delta_w_temp.hue: null, or a hue-word in Alex's own idiom only when he ratifies one

links._what: How this record connects to the prose record: Interzone entries by timestamp, studio logs and novel logs by file, with the relation named. This block carries the interoperation between the .jsonl stream and the .md streams.

md_logs.ref: file path or null while the log is unwritten
md_logs.relation: how the record and the log stand to one another

time._what: Required when ts is null: the honest statement of the time at the precision the record actually supports (time-honesty rule).
time.basis: what the stated precision rests on

required_envelope.actor: operator | archivillus | system - who performed the act, not who narrated the rendering
required_envelope.event: event type, from dictionaries/event_types (see dictionaries below)
required_envelope.id: unique record id (ULID preferred: sortable by time), never reused
required_envelope.recorded_at: when the record was written - may differ from ts for analog / off-computer work
required_envelope.seq: integer, position in this shard only, strictly increasing
required_envelope.session_id: the working stretch this belongs to; a pause of about 60 minutes on the same subject does not split a session
required_envelope.shard: origin of this file, e.g. historiotheque, experimental-novel, field, main
required_envelope.ts: when the event happened, ISO 8601 with local offset, e.g. 2026-10-17T23:02:00-04:00
required_envelope.v: schema version of this record, e.g. 1

status: ALPHA - adopted for the first official log, 2026-10-18. Supersedes the 2026-10-17 proposal for working use; the proposal file stands as the dated record of the proposal.
